From Brendan's journey interview (Sep 29, 2026): account first, then help at a workshop; mentoring Pods in a cycle comes from there. Buttons are new this cycle. Placeholders: any requirements.
description: Mentors at The Upskilling Labs are people who do the work, there to help a team when it gets stuck: for one workshop or a whole Build Cycle.

title: Know something?
Pass it on.
hero.alt: The Mentor button: the orb mark on ink, ringed by THE UPSKILLING LABS and MENTOR

intro.lede: Mentors are people who do the work, around when a Pod gets stuck. You wouldn't be teaching. You'd be the person in the room who's done it before.
intro.terms: A single workshop, or a whole cycle. You choose.
intro.status: Start by helping at a workshop.

met.$comment: For someone who met a wearer and wants to know who that was and how to think of them (most people who land here). The lede doubles as the spoken line the role's training gives wearers, so the page and the person say the same thing (design/research/role-explainers.md).
met.lede: They're a Mentor: someone who does this kind of work, there to help a team over a wall when it gets stuck.

know.title: A volunteer.
know.body: Giving one workshop, or a whole Build Cycle.

know.title: Not teaching.
know.body: The person in the room who's done it before.

know.title: A role, not a certification.
know.body: The button says who to ask when a team is stuck.

met.where: You'd meet one at a workshop at the public library, beside a team that's stuck, or at the Showcase. Ask them what they do.

items.title: Drop in.
items.body: They sit with a Pod when it's stuck, and ask what it's tried.

items.title: Unblock.
items.body: They share what they know from doing the work: a shortcut, a pattern, a person to ask.

items.title: Watch them ship.
items.body: They're there at the Showcase when the Pod shows what it built.

items.title: You choose the time.
items.body: A single workshop, or a whole cycle.

items.title: Nothing to prepare.
items.body: You're there when a Pod gets stuck, not at the front of a room.

items.title: Side by side.
items.body: Beginners and experts, working on the same real problem.

items.title: Free, always.
items.body: Nothing to pay, and nothing to sell.

path.title: Bring what you know. Leave with a Pod that shipped.

steps.title: Create your account.
steps.body: Your free Upskilling account: sign in with Google, and tell us what you know.

steps.title: Help at a workshop.
steps.body: Pick one to lead or help at. It's how most Mentors start.

steps.title: Mentor Pods in a cycle.
steps.body: When a Pod gets stuck, you're the person who's done it before. New this cycle: your Mentor button.

steps.title: Keep showing up.
steps.body: Come back for the next Pod, or the next cycle. It gets easier every time.

button.title: The one who's done it.
button.body: Worn when you're with a Pod, so people know who to ask. It marks a role, not a certification.

items.a: No. Mentors are around when a Pod gets stuck. There's nothing to prepare.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: A single workshop, or a whole cycle. You choose.
People who do the work, in any field. There are no formal requirements: what you bring is judged by how it works in practice.
Not really. There's no curriculum to get through. Teams work on a real problem and learn what they need along the way.

join.title: Pass it on.
join.lede: It starts with your free Upskilling account. Then pick a workshop to help at.
